# Pack: ubx-nav

u-blox UBX frames of the message class NAV (0x01), from the message definitions
of `https://github.com/semuconsulting/pyubx2` (`src/pyubx2/ubxtypes_get.py`, `ubxtypes_set.py`, `ubxtypes_poll.py`) at v0.0.0-fixture,
commit `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`. Public. Generated by `tools/gen/ubx2pack.py`; do not edit
`pack.def`, this file, `PROVENANCE.md`, `model/ubxnav.def` or the vectors by hand.

Status: Built. Generated and checked by the generator's own serializer and codec.

## The message

`wire bits`, `bit_order lsb`, `word_bytes 1`; hex text. One UBX frame without
its checksum; numbers are little-endian:

| Bytes | Content | In the pack |
|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | sync characters 0xB5 0x62 | common `when` |
| 2 | class, 0x01 | common `when` |
| 3 | id | per-kind `when` |
| 4-5 | payload length in bytes | per-kind `when` = the definition's fixed length |
| 6 … | payload | the kind's `field` lines, at their offsets |

The message is the frame without its checksum, in both directions: decode takes
the sync characters, header and payload, and encode writes them. A framer adds
the two checksum bytes before sending and checks them on receipt: an 8-bit
Fletcher checksum over class, id, length and payload (a running sum A of the
bytes and a running sum B of A, each modulo 256), written after the payload.
That is the item "Layered wires and framing" of `docs/roadmap.md`. A message
whose identity includes the first payload byte (the MGA messages) has a per-kind
`when` on that byte. Where the source chooses among definitions of one identity
by the value of one payload byte (`ubxvariants.py`: a version or type byte), the
kind it chooses that way has a `when` on that byte; the other definitions of the
identity are told apart by their length.

## Messages

A definition is the receiver's output (GET), a command to it (SET, kind suffix
`_set`) or a request (POLL, suffix `_poll`), as the source groups them.

| Kind | Definition | Mode | Identity | Payload bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nav_pvt` | NAV-PVT | GET | 0x01 0x07 | 52 |
| `nav_mixed` | NAV-MIXED | GET | 0x01 0x50 | 38 |
| `nav_velned` | NAV-VELNED | GET | 0x01 0x12 | 24 |
| `nav_variantb` | NAV-VARIANTB | GET | 0x01 0x53 | 5 |
| `nav_variant` | NAV-VARIANT | GET | 0x01 0x53 | 5 |
| `nav_variant_l` | NAV-VARIANT-L | GET | 0x01 0x53 | 9 |
| `nav_posllh` | NAV-POSLLH | GET | 0x01 0x02 | 52 |

## What is mapped

| Definition type | Transform | Model type |
|---|---|---|
| `U1` … `U8`, `X1` … `X8`, `E1` … `E4`, `L` | `uint` | int |
| `I1` … `I8` | `twos` | int |
| `R4`, `R8` | `f32`, `f64` | float |
| `C<n>` (text of a fixed length) | `ascii` | string |
| an integer with a scale | `uscale` / `sscale` with the scale as an exact fraction | float |
| a bit field (`_bit`) | each named bit group as its own field, from the least significant bit | int |
| a group with a fixed repeat count (`_grp`) | its fields once per repeat, `_01`, `_02`, … appended | as the field |
| `A<n>` (a byte array) | one `uint` byte per element, `_01` … appended | int |
| an unsigned integer wider than 8 bytes | 8-byte `uint` parts, `_01` … appended, the last part shorter | int |

Keys are `ubxnav.<kind>_<field>` in lower case. A scale the source states is
applied; the source states no unit, so the module declares none (`-`).

Scaled fields:

| Kind | Field | Transform |
|---|---|---|
| `nav_pvt` | `headVeh` | `sscale:45/4194304` |
| `nav_pvt` | `pDOP` | `uscale:1/100` |
| `nav_mixed` | `cno_01` | `uscale:16` |
| `nav_mixed` | `cno_02` | `uscale:16` |
| `nav_posllh` | `headVeh` | `sscale:45/4194304` |
| `nav_posllh` | `pDOP` | `uscale:1/100` |

### Core keys

pyubx2 states a scale for a field but rarely its unit or meaning. A field binds
a core or track key only where a public source shows both:

- ublox_msgs (`https://github.com/KumarRobotics/ublox`, package `ublox_msgs`, commit `3a3e1c253722`, BSD;
  the commit the ros2-ublox-msgs pack uses): the .msg file of the message states
  the unit of the field in its comment, and says what the field is (the north,
  east or down velocity, the 2-D ground speed, the 2-D heading of motion, the
  latitude, longitude or height above the ellipsoid). The generator reads the
  file and binds a field only when the comment says so and states the unit the
  table below converts: mm/s or cm/s to m/s, 1e-5 degrees to degrees, 1e-7
  degrees to degrees, mm to m. Up is the negative of down. A heading of motion
  binds `course`, read as degrees from true north, as for a GNSS solution in a
  north-east-down frame.

| Kind | Field | Key | Transform | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nav_pvt` | `lon` | `lon` | `sscale:1/10000000` | NavPVT.msg `lon` [deg / 1e-7] |
| `nav_pvt` | `lat` | `lat` | `sscale:1/10000000` | NavPVT.msg `lat` [deg / 1e-7] |
| `nav_pvt` | `height` | `hae` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `height` [mm] |
| `nav_pvt` | `velN` | `track.vel_north_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `vel_n` [mm/s] |
| `nav_pvt` | `velE` | `track.vel_east_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `vel_e` [mm/s] |
| `nav_pvt` | `velD` | `track.vel_up_ms` | `sscale:-0.001` | NavPVT.msg `vel_d` [mm/s] |
| `nav_pvt` | `gSpeed` | `speed_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `g_speed` [mm/s] |
| `nav_pvt` | `headMot` | `course` | `sscale:1/100000` | NavPVT.msg `heading` [deg / 1e-5] |
| `nav_velned` | `velN` | `track.vel_north_ms` | `sscale:1/100` | NavVELNED.msg `vel_n` [cm/s] |
| `nav_velned` | `velE` | `track.vel_east_ms` | `sscale:1/100` | NavVELNED.msg `vel_e` [cm/s] |
| `nav_velned` | `velD` | `track.vel_up_ms` | `sscale:-0.01` | NavVELNED.msg `vel_d` [cm/s] |
| `nav_velned` | `gSpeed` | `speed_ms` | `uscale:1/100` | NavVELNED.msg `g_speed` [cm/s] |
| `nav_velned` | `heading` | `course` | `sscale:1/100000` | NavVELNED.msg `heading` [deg / 1e-5] |
| `nav_posllh` | `lon` | `lon` | `sscale:1/10000000` | NavPVT.msg `lon` [deg / 1e-7] |
| `nav_posllh` | `lat` | `lat` | `sscale:1/10000000` | NavPVT.msg `lat` [deg / 1e-7] |
| `nav_posllh` | `height` | `hae` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `height` [mm] |
| `nav_posllh` | `velN` | `track.vel_north_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `vel_n` [mm/s] |
| `nav_posllh` | `velE` | `track.vel_east_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `vel_e` [mm/s] |
| `nav_posllh` | `velD` | `track.vel_up_ms` | `sscale:-0.001` | NavPVT.msg `vel_d` [mm/s] |
| `nav_posllh` | `gSpeed` | `speed_ms` | `sscale:1/1000` | NavPVT.msg `g_speed` [mm/s] |
| `nav_posllh` | `headMot` | `course` | `sscale:1/100000` | NavPVT.msg `heading` [deg / 1e-5] |

Every other field stays a raw key, accuracies and times among them: the
sources above state no unit for it, or state one this pack does not convert.

### `requires`

Each kind requires up to 3 of its own keys, so an entity from another format
selects a kind only when it holds them.

## What is not mapped

Definitions with no kind:

| Definition | Mode | Identity | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| NAV-COUNTED | GET | 0x01 0x51 | a group repeated by field `numCh` |
| NAV-TEXT | GET | 0x01 0x52 | text that runs to the end of the payload |
| NAV-MIXED | SET | 0x01 0x50 | the same class, id and payload length as kind `nav_mixed` |
| NAV-PVT | POLL | 0x01 0x07 | an empty payload: a kind needs at least one field |

2 of them have a variable part: a group repeated by a count field or to the end
of the payload, or text that runs to the end. Stating one needs a repeated group
counted by a field, or a trailing field of the remaining length.

1 have the class, id and length of a kind above; the source tells the
variants apart by a version field or by the direction of the message, which a
`when` on the length alone cannot.

- The checksum (see The message), and frames whose payload length is not the
  definition's fixed length: such a frame selects no kind (`no-kind`).
- Enumerations are carried as integers; the bits of a bit field that the
  definition does not name are not mapped.

## Vectors

`vectors/rt-<class><id>-<kind>.json`: one same-format round trip per kind, the
frame written by a UBX serializer in the generator from sample values.

`vectors/x-*-to-geojson.json`: a frame converted to GeoJSON; the expected text
is written by hand from the field values.

8 vectors.
